children: , a full-stack quantum computing company, rose 12.05% in premarket, after it said it had built and tested the first end-to-end real-time quantum error-correction decoder that runs on a single off-the-shelf central processing unit.

Error correction is a core obstacle to useful quantum computing: physical qubits are fragile, and the classical computers that catch and fix their errors have tended to choke on the load, forcing the quantum machine to pause. IonQ said its approach lets one processor handle that work in the background without slowing execution.

In a preprint posted to arXiv, IonQ reported testing its dual-decoder design on benchmark circuits simulating up to 408 logical qubits and more than 31.5 million operations, with the decoding adding as little as 0.02% in delay. Research lead Nicolas Delfosse called running the decoder on a single CPU "a practical path to commercial-scale fault-tolerant quantum computing." The company tied the result to its Walking Cat architecture and its roadmap beyond 256 physical qubits toward systems controlling thousands.

title: IonQ Stock Jumps 12% on Quantum Error-Correction Milestone
